payload.statement: Brush painting is generally the more economical option for finishing a staircase, but the final quality depends heavily on the preparation carried out before the paint is applied.

payload.statement: Experienced painters know that preparation — sanding, sealing exposed end grain, preparing turned spindles and ensuring every surface is clean — contributes far more to the finished appearance than simply applying paint.

payload.title: Preparing a staircase before painting or spray finishing
steps: Wipe the staircase thoroughly to remove sanding dust and loose timber fibres.
Use a suitable cleaning solvent recommended for the finishing system to remove fine dust from the timber grain before coating.
Always follow the manufacturer's guidance regarding compatible cleaning products.
Confirm preparation is complete before the finishing process begins.

evidence.note: Before any painting or spraying begins, it is good practice to wipe the staircase thoroughly to remove sanding dust and loose timber fibres. In the Author's professional experience, using a suitable cleaning solvent reco...

candidates.source_span: Before any painting or spraying begins, it is good practice to wipe the staircase thoroughly to remove sanding dust and loose timber fibres. In the Author's professional experience, using a suitable cleaning solvent recommended for the finishing system can help produce a cleaner finish by removing fine dust from the timber grain before coating. Always follow the manufacturer's guidance regarding compatible cleaning products.
